roles.title: Communicator
roles.summary: Strong communication across audiences; listening; succinct reports.

capacities.title: Messaging
capacities.definition: Effective communication of information to various audiences using a variety of media, ensuring the information is tailored to the audience.

levels.1: When someone gives me clear talking points or a script, I can share those messages the way I was shown.
levels.2: I can choose the right information for a specific audience and deliver it in a way that fits them.
levels.3: I confidently shape and deliver messages myself across different audiences, channels, and tools.

capacities.title: Active listening
capacities.definition: Engaging with and focusing on a speaker to deeply understand what they convey; perceptive to body language and subtle cues to preempt issues and flesh out useful information.

levels.1: I listen carefully and ask follow-up questions when something is unclear.
levels.2: I show I am listening (including through body language) and keep asking questions until I really understand what the person means.
levels.3: I ask thoughtful questions, reflect what I heard, and leave people feeling understood and respected.

capacities.title: Reporting
capacities.definition: Synthesizing information and observations so others understand; presenting in appropriate formats for internal and external stakeholders.

levels.1: When asked, I can write up what I observed in a clear, factual way.
levels.2: I produce shorter reports that combine what I saw with simple analysis, using normal reporting tools or software.
levels.3: On my own initiative I share concise updates—what I saw, what it may mean for the work—and I can present that well to different audiences.

capacities.title: Fostering trust
capacities.definition: Building and maintaining trust through integrity, competence, openness, reliability, and interest in others’ well-being.

levels.1: Trust tends to build slowly with market actors, communities, and teammates.
levels.2: I gain trust faster with some groups than others, and I pay attention to how much trust exists in each relationship.
levels.3: I build trusting relationships quickly where needed and I actively check and maintain trust with different people.

capacities.title: Making connections
capacities.definition: Identifying synergies between third parties and linking them to forge productive new relationships.

levels.1: I know a limited circle of people in the sector and can only make a few useful introductions.
levels.2: I have useful contacts, spot good matches, and introduce people so they can start working together productively.
levels.3: I keep strong networks (including government and business), create new links that fit programme priorities, align interests, and follow up so introductions turn into real collaboration.

capacities.title: Mediation
capacities.definition: Assisting two or more parties to resolve conflict, overcome challenges or reach agreement.

levels.1: In simple disagreements with few people involved, I can help find a compromise; I am not always fully neutral.
levels.2: I stay neutral, keep the conversation moving, and help people reach agreement or calm a conflict.
levels.3: I stay neutral, help people find workable and creative solutions, and keep ownership with them—not with me.

roles.title: Businessperson
roles.summary: Marketing, finances and records, human resources—for credibility and advice.

capacities.title: Marketing
capacities.definition: Understanding consumer needs, offering products and services that satisfy these needs, and ensuring long-term satisfaction.

levels.1: I can run simple surveys to learn about the market and I understand why good customer relationships matter.
levels.2: I can run surveys, do basic analysis, help with simple promotions or adverts, and I grasp how value chains connect to programme goals.
levels.3: I understand the marketing mix (the five Ps); I can gather market insights and advise on marketing strategy and customer care.

capacities.title: Finances and record-keeping
capacities.definition: Keeping track of financial positions, transactions, inventories, and other business information for accountability and decision-making.

levels.1: With someone guiding me, I can keep simple business records and I see why accurate records matter.
levels.2: I can keep solid records and understand basics like cash flow and profit.
levels.3: I can handle more complex business settings and records, give sound basic finance advice, spot financial risks, and weigh value to the market before money decisions.

capacities.title: Human resources
capacities.definition: Selecting, training and managing company personnel.

levels.1: I can help deliver training for junior staff or community members and I have a sense of what makes a good employee.
levels.2: I can run small training sessions on my own for junior staff and advise on choosing junior staff.
levels.3: I can run trainings, advise on hiring and recruitment, and understand how incentives affect performance.

roles.title: Coach
roles.summary: Needs assessment, feedback, and action—with ownership by market actors.

capacities.title: Needs assessment
capacities.definition: Dialogue with a coachee so both become aware of and understand areas for improvement.

levels.1: I sometimes meet market actors and stakeholders to hear their problems and needs.
levels.2: I meet regularly with market actors and stakeholders to talk through issues and pin down specific needs.
levels.3: I engage often to uncover real needs and help people want to act on those needs.

capacities.title: Feedback
capacities.definition: Giving and receiving constructive criticism or encouragement based on observations to enhance future effectiveness.

levels.1: I give praise easily but I rarely give corrective feedback; I tend to accept feedback from others without pushing back much.
levels.2: I give balanced positive and corrective feedback to some people I support, and I change how I work when I receive feedback.
levels.3: I give clear, useful feedback that helps people improve; I actively ask for feedback and use it to improve interventions.

capacities.title: Stimulate action
capacities.definition: Helping the coachee reach conclusions, formulate plans, and execute them.

levels.1: I help people think about next steps, but plans often stay vague.
levels.2: I help people build concrete action plans and I check in on how things are going.
levels.3: I help people commit to improvement, co-create action plans, support them, and keep ownership on their side.

roles.title: Innovator
roles.summary: Ideas, learning, and collaboration for market improvement.

capacities.title: Trying ideas
capacities.definition: Originating ideas for self and others and testing those ideas.

levels.1: I sometimes suggest new ideas for myself or partners but struggle to carry them through; I usually need a manager to approve.
levels.2: I am curious, try new ideas at times, bounce back when something fails, and think outside the usual box.
levels.3: I regularly test new ideas, treat setbacks as learning, and look beyond standard ways of working for solutions.

capacities.title: Learning
capacities.definition: Reflecting on actions and progress to inform future action.

levels.1: I learn from my own tasks but I change slowly unless someone directs me to.
levels.2: I actively learn from my work and from others, and I adjust what I do based on what I learned.
levels.3: I reflect, capture lessons, seek new learning, compare results to what I expected, and apply sector lessons to decisions.

capacities.title: Collaboration
capacities.definition: Sharing information and working with colleagues to create innovations in the team’s work.

levels.1: I share and collaborate when I am asked, and I contribute to the team.
levels.2: I share what works, work through issues with internal and external colleagues, and am seen as helpful in teams.
levels.3: I share successes and failures openly, spot what blocks teamwork and address it, and step up to lead when needed.

roles.title: Political economist
roles.summary: Institutional, political, and economic analysis for strategy.

capacities.title: Institutional analysis
capacities.definition: How institutions affect markets and poor people; options for change.

levels.1: With guidance, I can gather facts about institutions and how they affect markets.
levels.2: I can map a market system in basic terms—who holds influence, how institutions fit together, and what that means for poor people.
levels.3: I critically map institutions (for example with a diagram), assign roles fairly, and suggest practical changes that help poor people.

capacities.title: Political analysis
capacities.definition: How political power shapes public policy, service delivery, and markets.

levels.1: I notice politics in markets and, with guidance, I can collect relevant information.
levels.2: I can describe current political situations objectively and explain how they affect markets.
levels.3: I analyse how power and politics shape markets and poverty, map relationships, and recommend changes that help poor people.

capacities.title: Economic analysis
capacities.definition: Economic cost and benefit of public policy around market development.

levels.1: With guidance, I can gather economic information and see how markets connect to poor people.
levels.2: I can organise simple evidence in spreadsheets with light analysis to explain a market situation.
levels.3: I build richer evidence in spreadsheets, compare options with cost–benefit thinking, and argue for changes that benefit poor people in markets.

attitudes.title: Observant
attitudes.description: Keep up with the pace of business; notice changes and update plans accordingly.

attitudes.title: Determined
attitudes.description: Maintain focus and motivation when changing behaviours and markets is difficult.

attitudes.title: Curious
attitudes.description: Constantly seek new information, challenges, and solutions.

attitudes.title: Analytical
attitudes.description: Make rigorous assessments and informed decisions.

attitudes.title: Outgoing
attitudes.description: Proactively engage with a variety of market actors and stakeholders.

attitudes.title: Regard for others
attitudes.description: Obtain fulfilment from the facilitation approach.

capacities.title: Organization
capacities.description: Work successfully with multiple stakeholders and many tasks at the same time.

capacities.title: Teamwork
capacities.description: Realise goals that cannot be achieved by a single person.

capacities.title: Data analysis
capacities.description: Pull insight from quantitative and qualitative data collected.

capacities.title: Influencing
capacities.description: Ensure others contribute to your goals.

capacities.title: Decision-making
capacities.description: Take reasonable actions based on well thought-out assessments.
